integration_issues.issue: MOCKED network failure on /api/today?day_offset=1 produces fabricated comparisons against zero rather than an unavailable/loading state. With current PV=20 and yesterday request aborted, vp-bal-pv-delta displays '+20,00 kWh ggü. gestern'; autarky displays '+90,0 %-Pkt.'. All 19 comparisons behave this way. No error is shown. Priority MEDIUM.

action_items: Preserve null/unavailable yesterday through valuesFor and Delta; show 'Gestern: –' or a loading/error state instead of treating a failed request as an actual zero-energy day.

Review mixed PV comparison sources: today uses live hardware day counters whereas yesterday uses integrated snapshots. Demo currently shows approximately 0.21 kWh today versus 1.354 kWh from today's integration; ensure the intended estimator/timezone basis is documented or consistent for real devices.
critical_code_review_comments: DayBalance.jsx valuesFor(yesterday) coerces missing yesterday into zeros, defeating Delta's missing-data guard. VerlaufPreview.jsx catches yesterday fetch errors silently.
finite(null) is true because Number(null) is zero; a null-preserving fix must also reject null/undefined explicitly.

Today's PV comes from ahoy/MPPT device counters; yesterday's PV comes from /api/today integration. This is a source-consistency risk, not a proven production hardware failure. The existing demo-source discrepancy is acknowledged by the distribution-bar hint.

rca of the issue: Reproduce: intercept/abort GET /api/today?day_offset=1, reload /verlauf-preview, allow live and current today responses. yesterday stays null because catch swallows the error. valuesFor(null) returns numeric zeros for every previous metric; Delta sees valid numbers and renders today's full value as a change. Mitigation: retain availability state and avoid numerical coercion until both days are loaded; distinguish genuine zero from unavailable. No real backend 500 or integration outage observed.
